Commentary.Commentary: West Indies were largely disciplined in their bowling effort but the skipper, Jason Holder leaked some runs at the fag end of the innings which can prove to be costly. He gave away 36 runs in his last three overs. Ashley Nurse was the pick of the bowlers and he varied his pace nicely to keep the batsmen guessing. Gabriel was sharp too and impressed with his consistent lines and lengths. West Indies will fancy themselves to chase this down but the tourists are still in with a chance. Join us shortly for the chase.

A brilliant finish from Afghanistan has propelled them to a decent total on this two-paced track. A breezy 28-ball 41 by Gulbadin Naib along with a supporting knock from Mohammad Nabi was instrumental in pushing the visitors over the 200-run mark. However, the star of the show was Javed Ahmadi who played confidently and kept the scoreboard ticking. Although he would be disappointed to have missed out on his maiden ton, he did a good job for his side.
Full toss around middle and leg, Naib slogs it through mid-wicket for a single. AFGHANISTAN END ON 212/6.
Fuller outside off, Naib tries to dig it out but he is unable to make contact. The ball goes straight to the keeper and Nabi sends him back as Naib wants a single.

The ball flies straight to the keeper, Shai Hope who accepts it gleefully. The players appeal and the umpire obliges and Cummins has finally managed to get a wicket after three years. Actually, he didn't play for the Windies during that period but has done well on his comeback to the side. He gets finally rewarded for his consistent lines and lengths.

Rahmat Shah and Javed Ahmadi are batting really well. They have spent quite some time in the middle and now they will look to counter the bowlers to put some pressure back on the Windies.

We are ready to get underway. Noor Ali Zadran and Javed Ahmadi to open the batting for Afghanistan. Shannon Gabriel to start the proceedings with the ball. Two slips in place. Here we go...

West Indies skipper, Jason Holder says that it is not a bad toss to lose. Adds that there will be some good pace and bounce here and they  are playing four seamers. Announces that Devendra Bishoo and Rovman Powell miss out today. Feels that it is a new series and they need to be at their best. Mentions that they made some good strides in the Pakistan series. Ends by saying that Afghanistan is a fine side and they are not to be taken for granted.

Afghanistan skipper, Asghar Stanikzai says that he will like to bat first. Reckons that the wicket is quite different and looks a bit dry. Feels that it would be difficult to chase here. Mentions that they will look to post a total above 220 on the board and then look to defend it.
TOSS - AFGHANISTAN WIN THE TOSS AND OPT TO BAT!

On the other hand, the visitors need to improve drastically in order to challenge the hosts. They do have the potential and we might see them adjusting better to the 50-over format. Rahmat Shah is likely to back at the top of the order and he is a high quality player. The batsmen need to plan their innings sensibly to give their bowlers a chance. A much well-rounded performance is the need of the hour for them if they are to cause an upset. There is a bit of forecast for rain but hope it doesn't play spoilsport.

Hello and a warm welcome for the 1st ODI between West Indies and Afghanistan at the Darren Sammy National Cricket Stadium in Saint Lucia. A morale boosting 3-0 whitewash of the Asian side must have done the home side's confidence a world of good. They will aim to continue their dominance against a jaded Afghani side. Jason Holder will lead the Windies after being rested for the T20Is. Though it is an inexperienced team, there is some exciting talent in the ranks.
